tagline: Across to Hilton Head, with a refuge between.
intro: From SC 170, US 278 carries the byway about 22 miles toward Hilton Head Island and Sea Pines Circle, a busy multi-lane highway with landscaped medians. Between the mainland and the island lies Pinckney Island National Wildlife Refuge, much of it salt marsh and tidal creek, with walking trails through the protected ground.

The approach also passes Rose Hill, where construction of a Gothic house began before the Civil War and resumed after the Second World War. At the other end, the Sea Pines Company began its island development from an office trailer at the circle.

moments.title: Rose Hill Plantation House
moments.text: A steep roof and board-and-batten siding mark a house begun before the Civil War and finished in a later century.

moments.title: Pinckney Island National Wildlife Refuge
moments.text: Walking trails enter a refuge of salt marsh, freshwater ponds and forest between the mainland and Hilton Head.

moments.title: Sea Pines Circle
moments.text: The Sea Pines Company first worked from an office trailer at this intersection, where the scenic byway ends.
